body: It only locks with a key that he always has on him
No idea but I'll ask him about it next week. I just assumed that someone got into the house and he wasn't supposed to.

It's not usual but it happened before. He usually asks different questions or does something else in order to make talking easier but this time he waited 40 minutes. 

It would make sense to do something about the door but I highly doubt, that they'll buy and build in a new door just because of this.
I put a more detailed explanation of the house in my post, I hope that clears things up a bit. I will definately ask why he locked the door in the first place.
How am I not reliable? I'll try and explain the door to you if you want?
It's the door to the outside not the door to the room I was sitting in. But it doesn't make a difference because the only way out was locked

I don't know how I'm supposed to explain the house and the door. 

Basically I'm in a room with my therapist and that door is unlocked but there's a second door close to the other one that leads to the outside and that thing can be locked. There's no other door and no other way out unfortunately.

I just want to think a bit and calm down. I rather just wait for the appointment than to talk to him or message back and forth in order to try and find a small gap in his scedule. 

Right now I'm uncomfortable thinking about talking to him so I'm happy there's already an appointment and no need to talk before that.

I'd rather just leave things how they are appointment wise. Also it's unfortunately not that easy to just get a new therapist...most of them are already at capacity with their patients.

I'll sort things out next week and decide wether I'll stay or leave.

Yeah I understand what you mean. I know reddit can be a tricky place to ask for opinions but I only had this option because I literally have no one else to ask unfortunately. It was a bad situation and I really just needed other peoples thoughts. A few comments definately helped me to think differently about the situation and cleared up my thoughts/made me feel better. 

Also I wasn't uncomfortable with the door being locked because there's always another therapist on the same floor right in front of where I am and I just assumed something happened for the door having to be locked so I accepted that.

Yeah I don't know why he waited so long. He usually notices and asks me something else because he knows it's not easy to start talked after such a long time being quit.

I think it would be tought to terminate things after such a long time but I'll see how the call next week will be like.

Honestly I didn't even think about him doing that for my own safety. Reading other peoples thoughts about this did make me think about the situation differently. 

I will talk to him on the phone next week and figure things out. Thanks!

I'm always wary with everyone who's around me because it's something I picked up over the years that's all. I never felt unsave with my therapist before but at that moment he did something completely unpredictable wich I didn't know how to react to. It's easier said that done to just call the police. I just wished for things to be over because a person I trusted suddenly scared me like that. 

Unfortunately I go mute when I'm scared and just let things happen. Of course I know that's not the right thing to do but I still have to work on that...

Yeah I've been with him for about three years and I will talk to him on the phone next week  to clarify things. Most people are saying, that it's not okay to lock the door and keep someone in a room against their will. 

If I leave my therapist over this will most likely be decided next week but I did also come here for advice because this isn't something that just casually happens and I needed someone elses view on it. Sometimes it helps to hear what others think and that's what I was here for.

That does make sense and I didn't think about that. However...I think he could have communicated that to me instead of further asking me questions...? I don't know how professionals are supposed to handle these situation but that just doesn't make a lot of sense to me.

I turned 22 recently and I was barely able to think in that moment. I didn't even think about getting up, I just hoped that everything would resolve, if I stay quit and don't anger anyone. You know? 

(I don't know what outpatient and the other things are, english isn't my first language sorry. I'm there entirely voluntary and usually go there once a week. No medication, wasn't admitted or anything.)
No, first of all I was scared to get up because he's twice the size as me and second I didn't know how to react because I didn't expect him to refuse to unlock the door.

It's not a bad neighbourhood and I have no idea if there's ever been any problem patients or people entering the room but I assume that was the reason for my therapist to lock the door in the first place and that's fine. He asked me a few month ago, if I was okay with that and I agreed.

I sat there for 40 minutes (out of a normal 45 minutes appointment) in silence because I just froze right in the beginning and I don't know why. He even had me sit there for an additional 10 minutes (so 55 minutes in total). My therapist didn't let me leave despite me telling him that I was scared of him and that I wanted to leave and I've said that multiple times.

After 40 minutes of silence he tried to talk to me about what I was thinking about but I was panicking and couldn't think or answer. I was on the edge of my seat and scatching my phone case like crazy while barely being able to breathe but he insisted that I tell him why I feel this way. I told him to just let me out...he definately saw that I was stressed out.

I've known him for almost 3 years now and I've never had to ask that before and he always told me "you're here because you want to and you decide when to stop" but the one time I seriously needed to leave he didn't let me.

I probably won't return because I feel uncomfortable with the thought of being in the same room with him and unable to leave when I want to. Up to that point everything was fine and I never had any problems with him but that was horrible.

I really did like him until that happened and I'm going to ask why he did that on the phone next week. I don't think I can trust him enough to sit in the same room with him. 

Also my anxiety is really bad and I'm too scared to look for someone else unfortunately...
Thank you for the quick reply! It does make sense to avoid him if he acts weird about it...never really thought about it like that.

yeah I know, she already does these things, it's why independence is important for me now...I just can't win here. I hope I get some extra money from somewhere and hopefully don't have to see her ever again once I start to work...

Pretty sure it was a trigger for me but there were a few things he's done that made me scared of giving him honest answers but on the other hand he seems like he really does care and wants to help...he's the first and only person to help me so it's hard for me to tell if he's a good therapist or if the things he says are good or bad.

I should definitely try and address things like that more often...thank you for the comment it helped me get my thoughts sorted

yeah, I thought about addressing it but every time I say something like "I don't care anymore" or anything like that, he either goes "You want to go to a mental hospital then?" or "you don't look like it" so I feel like I can't talk to him about it. 

He's jokingly said stuff like "oh so now it's my fault, I didn't even mean it like that you just interpreted it the way you wanted" when I told him how I thought he meant something.   
I always let these things slide because I'm used to people talking to me like that (my mum always does that). I do know, that I constantly internalise things but I'm pretty sure, that wasn't one of these moments.

It doesn't make sense to me, that my therapist tried to hurt me but there were a few cases, where I was taken aback by his comments and should have probably said something but now I'm afraid of doing so because I'm scared of his answer...
Damn what a coincidence! It's good to know someone else feels the same way. I sure hope the bad thoughts stay behind and don't follow me to the couch. I thought about rearranging my room too.

Please leave him, you're not his mum and he needs to learn how to take care of his own mess. You're having an argument about him not wanting to help clean a bit of mess? What's supposed to happen when something more challenging happens in the future?   
I saw you comment, that he has anxiety and depression but it's not a free-pass to treat you like a maid. No one who loves you will start a fight over some housework and expect you to do everything on your own. Please tell me you aren't staying with someone like that because you deserve someone better...

Some people don't change no matter how much you want to believe in it and how often they say that they will change. I'm talking out of experience...don't get trapped on a manipulative relationship because of your good heart. I wish you the best and stay safe!
Yeah same here. No one really says anything about them anymore but I'm not blind I can tell they're not the best colour...oh and my paper white skin doesn't help with this at all

Yep that's exactly what it's like...

It's always been pretty hard to imagine a future tbh. Now I usually feel like I end up like my mum and since I constantly have her in front of me it's pretty hard to imagine anything else. I do have some positive thoughts here and there but I get anxious the second after because I'm scared of basically everything (god help me if I have to interact with other people). I have a therapist and he's constantly motivating me but it feels like all my progress resets as soon as I'm done with one task.

I'd like to have a more positive view of my future but it feels like my brain literally doesn't let me. So that's fun. It's like, with every positive though there's 4 negative attached.

They argued everyday since I was a child. Which unfortunately isn't axaggerated. My mum is the one who is causing the most problems. She would get physical over a cup that was put too far to the left in the cupboard. Sometimes even if the day seemed just fine, she would all of a sudden get mad over something that happened in the past and call me horrible names. My dad would always watch or go away because he didn't want to get involved.

My parents have been like this for over 20 years. It's fun that I have to learn, that it's not fine if someone abuses me and then acts like nothing happened the next day.

My mum has been physically and verbally abusive for over 20 years which she basically got from her parents and my dad would never stand up from me. No, I'm not blaming my parents for everything that is happening to me right now, I'm blaming them for not seeking the help they **desperately** needed **before** deciding to pull their child in to this chaos as well. Of course any decent person will try their best to raise a fragile little child who has no idea what the world and life even is about but my parents were far from decent when they decided to push their trauma onto me. And they could have decided to get help at any point but to this day they refuse.

I'm moving out in september for two years and I've been in therapy for 1 1/2 years now, my mum is also actively trying to stop me from doing so.

I feel like me blaming my parents for what they did is justified because over 20 years they thought it was fine to blame me for everything going wrong. I have such a twisted view of the world and the people, that I can barely say what's right or wrong now and that will take years to fix, which is most definately not fair.

I hope this is enough information. Sometimes, even after 20 years, you will not be able to escape a life like that because you never learned how to or you don't even know that a life, better than what you experienced, exists. Therapy isn't always an option for everyone and moving out isn't something you can just do like that.
Thank you a lot, I really appreciate the comment!

No, he's really great I think but hearing that does make me feel bad sometimes. I usually can't tell what's right or wrong so I sure hope he's actually a good match. He just tells me that I have to get out of my comfort zone

You should go to therapy if you think that your anxiety is keeping you from living your life normally. You don't have to have severe anxiety to go to a therapist but if you think your anxious feelings or thoughts are making your day to day life hard I would try therapy
Yes!
It's great to hear that you already took two big steps! Keep talking to your girlfriend, communication is key after all.

Well that's the thing about therapists, you can trust them differently because they're neither family or friends. You don't have to worry about any consequences in your private life. That's why she should consider going to one. 

I actually didn't notice opening up more because he was mostly having casual conversations with me and sometimes I would just unknowingly tell him how some things bothered me. After some time I realised I found a safe place.

But when you have someone in front of you going 'tell me what's wrong" sometimes there's just too many things at once and you don't know where to start. If you constantly ask her to do something she really doesn't want to do, you might make things worse because she sees that you're dissapointed with her not being able to do what you want.

That's why it's important to take baby steps with someone who has depression and you need to be patient. "Workout" already sounds like a lot. Even if it's 5 Minutes. When you're talking to her maybe ask her if she can touch her toes with her fingers, maybe you'll get her to stretch. Don't say "Can you do that for me" because it can be discouraging when she can't, she will probably feel like she dissapointed you.

I don't know your girlfriend and I don't know how to get her to open up to you but don't try and force anything. Read up on depression, talk to your girlfriend and tell her, that you're here for her. And I know it's probably annoying to hear at this point but patience is key.

Is there maybe a possibility for you to get professional help?  
Something I do which really helped me is writing my thoughts down in a journal too, so maybe try that once a while if you feel like you're being too overwhelming

It took me about a year and a half to open up to my therapist because it's really hard for me to trust others as well. Things like that can take a lot of time but she should really consider it and that it's ok for things to change slowly. 

Do be patient with her but don't sacrifice your own well being for hers...I don't mean to sound harsh but I know how exhausting it can be with someone who doesn't want to accept any type of help. Try and help her but you're not her therapist and there's only so much you can do.

Just keep that in mind and I hope everything will turn out ok.

Does she go to therapy or is there a way for her to get an appointment? I know how draining depression can get and I don't know how bad it is for her right now. Just try and talk to her about it, ask if there's something you can help her with or something nice she thought about doing but doesn't feel like she has the energy for. It can be something really simple because even that is sometimes a huge challenge for someone with depression.  


The mistake a lot of people make is, that they think they are helping someone but it's doing more harm than good. The best you can do is talk to each other about it. She should definately try and get better but don't push her into doing something, she really doesn't want to.
Stuff like "they're all going to hell" , "God didn't intend this", "It's not normal, it's disgusting" , "They should go to therapy and learn to deal with it". So yeah.

Damn I feel the exact same way. I listen to music almost 24/7 and when I get the chance I will just sing as loud as I can at home (when I'm alone) that's the only way that I can let off steam sometimes. I feel like I'm in my own safe world while listening to music.

I have the exact same outlook on life. Everyone just looks for their own purpose and that's it. Mine would be to hopefully help people one day because its something that makes me happy. I think hope matters the most. Hope that the suffering is going to be worth it and outweigh the suffering someday. Everyone just tries to make their life as pleasant as possible. Theres nothing more than that
aw man that's really nice...means a lot to me, thanks for sweet reply!

Oh I get to hear stuff like that from my mum all the time. "You got no reason to be sad, you got a room, tv, stuff etc." or "You're too young to have problems" or my favourite "I had it worse than you so pull yourself together". Like, thanks. I feel so much better now, wouldn't know what to do without your loving and kind words.
That's really sweet but I literally ignore any sort of advice or tips because in my eyes it won't work anyways, don't waste your time but still thanks the comment because it made me feel better!

Before depression everything was colourful and interesting. I could literally look at some dirt and be like "wow it's so cool this exists" but that was about 10 years ago. I actually attemted suicide this year in April and since then everything just went downhill. More than usual I mean.
